description: Two-part printed under-dash enclosure for the ha-carlink carrier PCB v0.1 (100 x 70 mm). The tray carries four M3 insert standoffs, a 14500 LiFePO4 cell trough behind a divider rib, a USB-C window and the OBD-II wire slot with a cable-tie strain-relief shelf; the lid clamps the board with four long bosses and retains the cell.

hardware.item: M3 heat-set insert (4.6 mm OD, up to 5.7 mm long)
hardware.notes: One per standoff; set insert_hole_d to 2.6 instead for self-tapping screws
Through a lid boss into its standoff insert
OBD-II pigtail through the shelf tie-slot pairs

hardware.item: 14500 LiFePO4 cell with leads crimped to a JST-XH housing

hardware.notes: Optional cell wrap/packing in the trough

printing_notes: Print both parts as exported without supports: the base floor-down, the lid outer-face-down. PETG or ASA is recommended for a car interior, 3 perimeters.
Press the four M3 heat-set inserts into the standoffs before fitting the board.
Assembly order: board onto the standoffs, cell into the trough with its lead through the divider notch into J2, lid on, then the four corner screws.
The USB and OBD-II slot positions come from the board design, not a measured board; check usb_z0/usb_h and obd_h against the real DevKitC-1 and terminal after the first print.
Lay the pigtail in the shelf's cable groove and tie it down through the two tie-slot pairs.
Set insert_hole_d to 2.6 for self-tapping screws instead of heat-set inserts.
Lift the lid off (four screws) to change the mini-blade fuse.
If the lid rim sits proud of the tray because a boss printed long, lower boss_extra (down to -2) and re-render the lid; the M3 x 30 screw only has headroom to shorten the boss, not lengthen it.
wall, floor_t, corner_r, standoff_h, cell_d and cell_l are shared parameters: set them identically on the base and the lid.
